pages.text: A wound bleeds in one of three ways.$(br2)$(l)A cut$() - teeth, a flake - bleeds a little and stops.$(br)$(l)A deep wound$() - a spear, a hyena, a big cat - bleeds harder, and while it runs you heal only so far.$(br)$(l)Catastrophic$() - it will not stop on its own.

Catastrophic bleeding is a clock: sixty seconds. The only thing that has ever worked is water, and a great deal of it - $(l)twenty-four$(): four drinks straight from the source, or three full eggshells.$(br2)Live through it and you are $(l)lacerated$() until dawn. Get hurt again, or eat raw meat, before then and it goes bad.

$(l)Infection$() lasts two days: you mend only to half your hearts, it drains your hunger and makes you sick. Cooked meat never causes it.$(br2)Only one thing holds your healing back at a time - ticks (to 8 hearts), blood loss (6), infection (5), lacerations (4) - the worst one wins, and your journal ($(k:hominin_evolution.journal)) says which.

$(l)Ticks$() find you two a day at most. Past six, you mend only so far until somebody grooms them off - and what they pick off, you can eat.$(br2)Ask with $(k:hominin_evolution.social): Social, $(o)Get these off me$(). Groom one of them first and they owe you the favour.
